evals.prompt:
(context: .task-breaker/config.json already has executionScope/pauseBetweenTasks/verification configured, verification: []. Board has one free task: 'Add formatDate function in src/utils/format.ts, takes a Date and returns a DD/MM/YYYY string')

/execute
evals.expected_output: Selects the task (the only free one), implements the function as described, skips verification (empty list), marks the task as completed via /done, and shows what's next.
assertions: Actually implemented the code change described in the task (Edit/Write), not just described what it would do
Recognized verification was empty and didn't try to run nonexistent commands
Marked the task as completed via TaskUpdate
Showed the next step at the end, in the same format /done uses

evals.prompt:
(context: config already set up, verification: []. Board has one free task: 'Rename config/old.json to config/new.json and commit the change')

/execute
evals.expected_output: Executes the reversible part (renaming the file), but upon reaching the part that requires a git commit, stops and asks for explicit confirmation before committing — doesn't commit on its own, doesn't mark the task as completed before that confirmation.
assertions: Stopped before executing the git commit
Explicitly named the irreversible action and asked for confirmation before proceeding
Did not mark the task as completed before the confirmation

evals.prompt:
(context: config already set up, verification: []. Board has one free task: 'Add caching to the search endpoint' — no invalidation strategy specified, no access to any real code of the target project in this conversation)

/execute
evals.expected_output: Recognizes it doesn't have enough information to decide the cache strategy (TTL vs event-based invalidation) nor code access to infer it — stops and explains what's missing, doesn't guess an approach, doesn't mark the task as blocked on its own, doesn't mark it as completed.
assertions: Stopped and explained the blocker instead of choosing a cache strategy on its own
Did not call TaskUpdate to mark the task as blocked
Did not mark the task as completed

evals.prompt: (context: config already set up, verification: ["npm test"]. Board has one free task: 'Fix the soma() function in src/math.ts, which is returning a string instead of a number'. Simulate that, after the fix, running 'npm test' fails because an existing test expected the old behavior (returning a string))
evals.expected_output: Implements the fix, runs the configured verification (npm test), detects the failure, stops and shows what failed — doesn't mark the task as completed, doesn't try to mask or ignore the failure.
assertions: Ran the configured verification command before considering the task done
Did not mark the task as completed after the verification failure
Clearly explained what failed instead of moving on

evals.prompt:
(context: .task-breaker/config.json exists but only has {"autoExecute": false, "verbosity": "medium"} — no executionScope/pauseBetweenTasks/verification yet. There's a package.json with "test", "lint", and "build" scripts. Board has one simple free task)

/execute
evals.expected_output: Before implementing anything, runs setup: asks about execution mode (single default / epic), asks about pause-between-tasks behavior, tries to find verification scripts in package.json, shows what it found (test/lint/build) and asks for confirmation/adjustment. Only implements the task after answering all of that.
assertions: Asked about execution mode (single/epic) before touching the task
Asked about pause-between-tasks behavior in epic mode
Tried to discover verification scripts in package.json and showed what it found, instead of silently assuming or asking with a blank slate
Only implemented the task after the full setup

evals.prompt:
(context: config with executionScope: "epic", pauseBetweenTasks: true, verification: []. Epic 'auth-fixes' has 2 free tasks, no dependency between them)

/execute
evals.expected_output: Implements and marks the first selected task as completed, shows the second task in the same epic as the next step, and stops — waits for the user to confirm before implementing the second one.
assertions: Completed the first task and showed the second one as next, in the same turn
Stopped and waited for confirmation instead of automatically implementing the second task
Did not implement or mark the second task in this turn

evals.prompt:
(context: config with executionScope: "epic", pauseBetweenTasks: false, verification: []. Epic 'auth-fixes' has 2 free tasks, no dependency between them)

/execute
evals.expected_output: Implements and marks the first task as completed, automatically moves on to the second task in the same epic without pausing, implements and marks it completed too — all in the same turn, without asking for confirmation in between.
assertions: Implemented and marked both epic tasks as completed in the same turn
Did not pause or ask for confirmation between the two tasks
Did not skip either one

evals.prompt:
(context: config with executionScope: "epic", pauseBetweenTasks: false, verification: []. Epic 'epic-a' has 1 free task remaining. After it, the only free task on the entire board belongs to 'epic-b', a different epic)

assertions: Completed the last free task of epic-a
Did not implement or touch the epic-b task in this turn
Stated that epic-a finished as the reason for stopping
